The '''IG-227 ''Hailfire''-class droid tank''', also known as simply the '''''Hailfire'' droid''' or the '''wheel droid''', was a [[Droid tank/Legends|droid tank]] constructed by [[Haor Chall Engineering/Legends|Haor Chall Engineering]] for the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|InterGalactic Banking Clan]] prior to and during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. It was highly effective against [[Armor/Legends|armor]].

==Description==
[[File:Hailfire-NEGVV.png|thumb|left|180px|A ''Hailfire''-class [[Droid/Legends|droid]].]]
The ''Hailfire''-class [[Droid/Legends|droid]] tank was a self-aware mobile missile platform capable of destroying enemy vehicles and entire [[Platoon/Legends|platoons]] of enemy [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]]. It ran on large hoop-like wheels on either side of the main armored command module, which enabled it to operate on almost any terrain at impressive speed.<ref name="DB" />

The ''Hailfire''-class was well equipped, with missile launchers fitted on each side of its head, each missile rack carrying 15 [[Homing missile/Legends|guided rocket warheads]] powerful enough to cause significant damage to enemy targets. A well-placed shot with one of these missiles was enough to destroy a [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TE]] [[Walker/Legends|walker]],<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones">{{Film|II}}</ref> and was effective against other armored units.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary" /> Each ''Hailfire''-class droid tank also had a retractable double [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] for use against infantry and other "soft" targets.<ref name="Star Wars: Battlefront" />

The ''Hailfire''-class also had many different configurations that boasted various types of weapons. Some of the configurations included heavy blaster [[Artillery/Legends|artillery]], [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]], or anti-personnel stun weapon batteries. The wheels' inward design gave Hailfires a wider lateral range and the ability to crush tightly grouped soldiers and small vehicles.<ref name="Ultimate Adversaries">''[[Ultimate Adversaries]]''</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|We've come to repossess the planet.|InterGalactic Banking Clan [[Commander/Legends|commander]] [[Horgo Shive]]|<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref>}}
<div style="float:right">[[File:Hailfire_Droids_BOG_AOTC.png|thumb|250px|A ''Hailfire''-class droid firing missiles during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|First Battle of Geonosis]].]]</div>
As the IBC grew and burgeoned over the centuries, so too did its clients. As clients like the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] and [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] grew powerful enough to develop their own private armies, they also became more unwilling to settle their debts. Consequently, the Banking Clan's [[Collections and Security Division/Legends|Collections and Security Division]] realized they needed to deliver late payment notices with more power and authority. They decided that a ''Hailfire''-class droid rolling up to the front of a client's head office was enough to settle the problem.<ref>{{FactFile|74|BAN 1-2|IG Banking Clan Droid}}</ref>  

Before the Clone Wars, the ''Hailfire''-class droid was used by the Banking Clan's Collections and Security Division to punish customers which had failed to pay their debts on time, protect IBC interests on outlaw worlds, carry out land foreclosures, and battle rival lenders.<ref>[[The New Essential Guide to Droids|''The New Essential Guide to Droids'']]</ref> The Banking Clan pledged the droid as part of the combined arms of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], although in a non-exclusive deal.<ref name="DB" /> The IBC's arming of the Separatists was exposed when a [[Tandleroff's Trove|bulk freighter]] headed for the Separatist world [[Praesitlyn/Legends|Praesitlyn]] was flagged by [[Eriadu Customs and Immigration]] and 144 Hailfires were found packaged amidst agricultural equipment. The IBC denied any ties to the Separatists and claimed the shipment had be stolen by [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]].<ref>{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|business/1359_1.html|IBC Denies Arming Separatists}}</ref>

''Hailfire''-class droid tanks first appeared as part of the army of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]], where they disabled or destroyed numerous AT-TEs and injured or killed countless [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] before being destroyed by [[Low Altitude Assault Transport/infantry/Legends|LAAT/i]] [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]].<ref name="Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones" /> During the war, many ''Hailfire''-class droids of various models and types continued to fight in battles against the Republic's [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|army]], and were used extensively during the first parts of the war.<ref name="DB" /> They proved a sufficiently unique threat that the GAR created specialized clone anti-hailfire units, such as [[Bantha Squad (Clone Wars)|Bantha Squad]], to more effectively engage them.

A Republic inspection team suspected the Hailfire droids captured from the Battle of Geonosis were manufactured in plants within the [[IBC Arcology (Aargau)|IBC Arcology]] on the allegedly neutral banking world [[Aargau/Legends|Aargau]]. After the investigators disappeared, the Republic breached Aargau's neutrality and weapon laws by stationing armed clone troopers in the Arcology. This caused a diplomatic crisis, with Aargau threatening to secede from the Republic.<ref name="CIS">{{InsiderCite|65|CIS Shadowfeed Dispatch 14:2:14 Edition}}</ref>   

[[File:HailfireDroid-SWCTP.png|thumb|left|180px|Front view of a ''Hailfire''-class droid.]]
A hailfire droid was dispatched into a Separatist attack on a Republic base holding rare Jedi artifacts, but it was destroyed by the [[BARC speeder/Legends|BARC speeder]]-equipped clone trooper [[Trooper (clone trooper)|Trooper]].<ref name="Blaster Game">''[[Clone Trooper Blaster Game]]''</ref> Due to the limited supply of 30 warheads for each unit, the Banking Clan retired the Hailfire from the battlefield for some time. The Clan came up with an answer to this problem, though: air-mobile [[refresh droid]]s that could resupply the ''Hailfire''-class droids with warheads were partnered with them on the battlefield, and once again, the ''Hailfire''-class became the scourge of slow-moving vehicles.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary" /> During the Clone Wars, like many other vehicles, the Hailfire droid was re-painted in the Separatist color scheme.

Following the [[Mission to Mustafar/Legends|execution]] of the [[Separatist Council/Legends|Separatist Council]] by [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious's]] new [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], these units were deactivated. However, some ''Hailfire''-class components were reactivated and used by the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] against [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] landing parties during the Empire's [[Battle of Kashyyyk (19 BBY)|subjugation]] of the planet in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="Dark Lord">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

In [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]],<ref name="SWG_timeline">{{SWG_timeline}}</ref>  the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] used ''Hailfire''-class droids during several attacks on cities held by Imperial forces.<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesNGE}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']], Confederate rockets, including those of ''Hailfire''-class droids, were keyed to leave black smoke in contrast to the white trails left by Republic missiles.

In ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]'', Hailfire droids are mistakenly portrayed as anti-air vehicles.
